Elon Musk publicly showcased a prototype that blends a Tesla Roadster with SpaceX‑derived thrust technology. [SRC-2e795e58ccf9]
On 15 Oct 2026, during a livestream from a SpaceX test site in Texas, the vehicle drove up a steep, curved ramp, went upside‑down, performed a mid‑air flip and landed on its wheels – a stunt described in detail by Blueprint Newspapers [ SRC-2e795e58ccf9 ].
The Energy Tribune report also notes the ramp launch and wheel landing but does not mention the flip [ SRC-2d5ea846f910 ].

Musk labeled the vehicle a “flying car” and said the project is a collaboration between “the world’s best car company and the world’s best rocket company.” Both articles state that production is planned for 2028. [SRC-2e795e58ccf9]

The propulsion system is described only in broad terms: ultra‑high‑pressure air tanks feed thrusters that push the car into the air. [SRC-2e795e58ccf9]

Spread the word
Elon Musk, chief executive officer of Tesla, has unveiled a new version of the company’s long-awaited Roadster electric sports car, demonstrating a prototype capable of performing aerial stunts using technology developed in collaboration with his aerospace company, SpaceX.
The vehicle was showcased on Thursday, October 15, 2026, during a livestreamed event at a SpaceX testing facility in Texas, United States. The demonstration attracted widespread attention after the car drove along a curved ramp, travelled upside down before launching into the air, performed a mid-air flip and landed on its wheels. Blueprint reports
Musk described the development as evidence that flying cars could become a reality, although questions remain about the vehicle’s final capabilities, safety and regulatory approval.
“Flying cars are real,” Musk said during the event, while acknowledging that the project’s success was not guaranteed.
The demonstration was broadcast on Tesla’s social media account and featured a series of displays intended to highlight the vehicle’s unusual engineering and performance.
SpaceX technology powers aerial stunts
According to Musk, the Roadster uses ultra-high-pressure air tanks and thrusters to propel itself into the air. The system draws on technology associated with SpaceX, the aerospace company he also leads.
The vehicle’s engineering combines conventional electric-car technology with specialised equipment designed to enable manoeuvres that would be impossible for an ordinary road car.
During the presentation, Tesla’s vehicle engineering team also explained that a suction system beneath the car helps it maintain contact with a surface during certain manoeuvres, including driving upside down.
The prototype subsequently demonstrated another aerial stunt, launching over a line of Tesla vehicles before returning to the ground.
The displays were designed to demonstrate the potential of combining Tesla’s electric-vehicle engineering with SpaceX’s experience in propulsion and aerospace technology.
Musk described the project as the product of collaboration between what he called the world’s best car company and the world’s best rocket company.
However, the demonstration does not necessarily mean that all the features shown will be available in every production model. The specifications, practical limitations and availability of the most advanced features will depend on the final vehicle and the version offered to customers.
Roadster targets 2028 production
Musk said production of the new Roadster is expected to begin in 2028, extending a project that has experienced years of delays.
Tesla first unveiled plans for the second-generation Roadster in 2017, promising a high-performance electric sports car with exceptional acceleration and a long driving range.
The original production timetable was subsequently pushed back, leaving customers who reserved the vehicle waiting for the next-generation model.

Elon Musk unveils futuristic flying car concept at SpaceX facility
Photo: Collected
Tesla chief executive Elon Musk has unveiled a new Roadster sports car equipped with thrusters, describing it as a “flying” car during a livestreamed event at SpaceX’s facility in Texas.
The demonstration took place on Thursday at a SpaceX test facility and was broadcast on Tesla’s X account. The vehicle launched from a steep ramp before landing on its wheels.
“Flying cars are real,” Musk said during the event.
He cautioned that the vehicle’s “success is not guaranteed”, but added that “it will probably work”.
Musk said, “The car was equipped with ultra-high-pressure air tanks designed to propel it into the air.”
He described the project as the result of collaboration between “the world’s best car company and the world’s best rocket company”, referring to Tesla and SpaceX.
Musk said, “The vehicle would enter production in 2028.”
Despite decades of interest, flying cars have yet to achieve widespread commercial use, with technical and regulatory hurdles continuing to challenge the sector.
American aviation pioneer Glenn Curtiss unveiled an early flying-car prototype in 1917. The concept has attracted renewed attention in recent years as advances in electric motors and high-performance batteries have opened up new possibilities for airborne vehicles.

Reusable Rocket Patents
Propulsive landing, grid fins, booster catch, and reusable TPS IP; reusable rocket patent landscape for launch-vehicle startup founders.
FAQ
Who are the major reusable rocket patent holders and what innovations do SpaceX, Blue Origin, and Rocket Lab protect? Reusable rocket patents cover propulsive vertical-landing innovations; aerodynamic-control and descent innovations; recovery-mechanism innovations; and reuse/refurbishment innovations — with IP held by reusable-launch leaders, suborbital pioneers, and small-launch recovery specialists. MAJOR REUSABLE-ROCKET PATENT HOLDERS: SPACEX (deep estate): Falcon 9 first-stage vertical-takeoff-vertical-landing VTVL, propulsive landing-burn (boostback, entry, landing burns), titanium grid fins for hypersonic/supersonic control, deployable landing legs, autonomous spaceport droneship sea landing, supersonic retropropulsion, engine relight/restart, and the Starship/Super Heavy 'chopsticks' tower-arm booster catch (Mechazilla). BLUE ORIGIN: New Shepard suborbital vertical landing (ring fin, drag brakes, throttleable BE-3), and New Glenn reusable first stage (landing on a downrange vessel). ROCKET LAB: Electron first-stage recovery via parachute and (formerly) mid-air helicopter capture, re-entry thermal protection for a small stage, and the Neutron reusable design with an integrated fairing and 'Hungry Hippo' captive fairing. OTHERS: Stoke Space (full reusability, actively-cooled metallic heat-shield + differential-throttle second stage), Relativity (Terran R reusable), and legacy reusability heritage (DC-X, Space Shuttle TPS) that forms prior art.
What propulsive-landing, guidance, and aerodynamic-control innovations are patentable? Landing-guidance and trajectory-optimization innovations; propulsive landing-burn innovations; aerodynamic descent-control innovations; and deep-throttle/relight innovations represent core reusable-rocket patent domains. GUIDANCE / TRAJECTORY PATENTS: powered-descent guidance and onboard real-time trajectory optimization (convex-optimization 'G-FOLD'-style fuel-optimal landing, successive convexification), divert/retargeting logic, sensor fusion (radar altimeter, GPS/INS, lidar) for precision landing, and autonomous landing-site selection. LANDING-BURN PATENTS: boostback and entry/landing burn sequencing, hoverslam/suicide-burn timing (zero velocity at zero altitude to save propellant), throttle scheduling, and propellant-margin management. AERODYNAMIC-CONTROL PATENTS: grid fins (lattice control surfaces) and their actuation, deployment, and hypersonic heating management; ring fins, drag brakes, and ballutes; reaction-control thrusters for attitude during coast; and flip/transition maneuvers (e.g. Starship belly-flop to vertical). PROPULSION-FOR-REUSE PATENTS: deep-throttling engines (single-engine landing of a multi-engine stage), reliable in-flight relight/restart, autogenous pressurization for restart, and gimbal/thrust-vector contro
